scenes.heading: Rounding and estimating
scenes.sub: Quick, nearly-right answers that catch mistakes
scenes.say: You don't always need an exact answer. About fifty thousand people at the footy is clear enough. Rounding makes numbers simpler, and estimating helps you catch mistakes.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: At 4682 m, with bus stops at 4600 m and 4700 m, walk to the closer one
scenes.science: 4682 rounded to the nearest hundred is 4700
scenes.breaks: In real life you might pick either stop when exactly halfway. In maths, halfway always rounds up.
scenes.say: Picture bus stops every hundred metres. You're at four thousand, six hundred and eighty-two metres, between the stops at four thousand six hundred and four thousand seven hundred. You walk to the closer one: four thousand seven hundred. In maths, if you're exactly halfway, you always go up.
scenes.caption: Picture bus stops every 100 m. You're at 4682 m, between the stops at 4600 m and 4700 m. Walk to the closer one: 4700. In maths, if you're exactly halfway, you always go up.

scenes.heading: How to round
steps: Look at the digit on its right
5 or more: add 1. 4 or less: keep
scenes.say: Here's how to round. Find the rounding digit. Look at the digit just to its right. If it's five or more, add one to the rounding digit. If it's four or less, leave it. Then fill every place after it with zeros.

scenes.heading: Rounding with a 9
scenes.question: Round 2950 to the nearest hundred.
scenes.say: Round two thousand, nine hundred and fifty to the nearest hundred. The rounding digit is nine, and the decider is five, so round up. Nine plus one is ten, so write zero and carry one. The answer is three thousand.
scenes.caption: Round 2950 to the nearest hundred. The rounding digit is 9, and the decider is 5, so round up. 9 + 1 = 10, so write 0 and carry 1. The answer is 3000.

scenes.heading: Estimating
scenes.question: Estimate 587 × 42.
scenes.say: Estimate five hundred and eighty-seven times forty-two. Round each number to its leading digit: six hundred and forty. Six times four is twenty-four, then add three zeros: twenty-four thousand. The exact answer is twenty-four thousand, six hundred and fifty-four, so the estimate is close.
scenes.caption: Estimate 587 × 42. Round to the leading digit: 600 and 40. 6 × 4 = 24, then add three zeros: 24 000. The exact answer is 24 654, so the estimate is close.

scenes.heading: Estimates catch mistakes
points: About 10 times too big: extra zero
scenes.say: Estimates catch mistakes. If a calculator says seven times four hundred and twelve is twenty-eight thousand, eight hundred and forty, estimate: seven times four hundred is two thousand eight hundred. That's ten times smaller, so there's an extra zero. The real answer is two thousand, eight hundred and eighty-four.
scenes.caption: Estimates catch mistakes. If a calculator says 7 × 412 = 28 840, estimate: 7 × 400 = 2800. That's ten times smaller, so there's an extra zero. The real answer is 2884.

points: Decider digit is just to the right
scenes.say: Quick recap. The decider digit is just to the right of the rounding digit. Five or more, raise the score. Four or less, let it rest. Always round the original number once. And estimate before you press equals. Now try the practice questions!
